ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, OA and OB are two radii of the circle $O$, and point C is on the circle $O$. If $\angle AOB = 80^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle ACB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since OA and OB are two radii of the circle O, with point C on the circle O, and $\angle$AOB=80°, \\
it follows that $\angle$ACB=$\frac{1}{2}\angle$AOB=$\boxed{40^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, there is a circle with O as the center, and A, B, and C are all on the circumference. Line segments OA and OB connect from the center O to A and B on the circle respectively, and are two radii; line segments CA and CB connect to point C, forming the inscribed angle ∠ACB. The problem statement gives ∠AOB = 80°. Reasoning: ∠AOB is the central angle intercepting the same arc AB, and ∠ACB is the inscribed angle intercepting arc AB. According to the inscribed angle theorem, the inscribed angle subtended by the same arc is equal to half of the central angle, so ∠ACB = 1/2 × 80° = 40°.
